# Retired figures and corrected claims — the authority for the CI guard
# "no retired figures or corrected claims regressed".
#
# Every non-comment, non-blank line is an extended regular expression (ERE).
# If one matches published content, CI fails: the claim was corrected once and
# must not come back.
#
# Read by .github/workflows/portfolio-checks.yml, which checks index.html and
# order-engine/index.html. This file is the list; the workflow is only one
# consumer of it. Anything else that publishes these claims — a resume, a
# profile, a cover letter — should be checked against this list by hand, since
# CI cannot reach documents that live outside the repo.
#
# Each pattern must be matched by at least one example in
# retired-claims.canary.txt, which proves the pattern still catches the thing it
# was written for. A pattern that matches nothing is a guard that passes for the
# wrong reason.
#
# To retire a new claim: correct the content, add the pattern here with what
# replaced it and why, and add the original wording to the canary.

# SPSC throughput was published as "118M ops/sec" and "118 M/s".
# Corrected in 5388e03 to a median ~103M ops/sec (93-105M across 3 runs), when
# the benchmarks were reproduced on Windows/MSVC.
118 ?M

# Order-to-fill p99 was published as 1.9 us, alongside a 1.0 us p50.
# Corrected in 5388e03 to 2.1-2.3 us p99 and ~0.9 us p50, same reproduction.
1\.9[[:space:]]?µs

# "O(1) cancel" asserted a complexity bound the implementation does not provide.
# Removed in 17a7c10, replaced with what the code actually does: indexed
# price-level lookup for cancellation over FIFO order storage per level.
O\(1\) cancel

# "built from scratch to survive market-open bursts" named a workload the engine
# was never benchmarked against. Removed in 17a7c10, replaced with "designed and
# benchmarked for bursty order flow".
market-open
